did_you_know.text: Was the "Cushite woman" Zipporah, Moses' Midianite wife, or another woman? Many commentators see "Cushite" as a picturesque description, for her beauty or dark complexion, referring to Zipporah.
The description of Moses as "more humble than any man" is a unique self-description in the Bible, raising fascinating questions about the authorship and divine inspiration of the Torah.

The phrase "mouth to mouth I speak with him" highlights Moses' prophecy as unique and immediate, without the need for dreams or riddles like other prophets, emphasizing his direct connection with God.
Miriam's leprosy (tzara'at) is traditionally understood as a punishment for *lashon hara* – slanderous or harmful speech – serving as a severe warning about the importance of proper speech.

The fact that the entire nation of Israel, a camp of hundreds of thousands of people, halted its journey and waited seven days until Miriam returned to the camp, underscores her importance and honor in the eyes of the people.
